short: Forty-four years of war ended a millennium of native Chinese rule over the south.
full:
The Song had helped the Mongols destroy the Jin in 1234 and were attacked the following year. What followed was the longest campaign the Mongols ever fought. The terrain defeated cavalry: rivers, paddy, malaria, and a belt of walled cities the Song had spent a century fortifying. Möngke Khan died in 1259 at the foot of Diaoyu fortress in Sichuan without taking it, which pulled his brothers home to fight over the succession.

Kublai returned to the problem in the 1260s with different tools. The twin fortresses of Xiangyang and Fancheng on the Han River held out from 1268 until 1273, falling only after Persian engineers built counterweight trebuchets capable of throwing stones through their walls. That opened the Yangtze. Kublai also built a fleet, largely crewed by defectors, and Hangzhou surrendered in 1276. Loyalists fled south with two child emperors in turn; the last of them drowned at Yamen in 1279. For the first time all of China was ruled from outside it.
